# ASP initial discovery benchmark rationale

The manifest is intended to be run with `C:\Programming\Projects` as the benchmark root, so every task uses the portable repository path `ASP`. Expectations were derived from the checked-out ASP repository on 2026-07-27. They describe file-set outcomes, not an exact selection order.

## Evidence and expectations

| Task | Why the expectation is valid | Why the budget is bounded this way |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `application-startup` | `package.json` declares `server.js` as the main file and maps `npm start` to `node server.js`; `README.md` independently documents `npm start`, so either is valid command evidence. `server.js` calls `startServer()` only when it is executable. `public/index.html` loads `public/app.js`, so either browser file can establish client bootstrap. | Five selected files keep the result focused. The measured fresh bound is the 26-file scan plus up to five selected files; indexed and hybrid modes override it to fourteen reads. |
| `architecture-overview` | `server.js` owns HTTP, Socket.IO, state, and API wiring. Media is split among provider search, source resolution, and player adapters, so `required_files_any` accepts any representative media module instead of assuming one model-selected subsystem. Browser files remain relevant but are not mandatory because the published index does not expose one among this task's selectable candidates. | Seven selections and sixteen indexed/hybrid reads cover multiple layers plus limited supporting context without rewarding repository-wide enumeration. |
| `bug-localization-library-refresh` | `public/videos.js` increments `videosLoadSequence` and rejects an obsolete response. `test/library-ui.test.js` has the focused test named “out-of-order video responses cannot overwrite a newer library render.” The license and global-access helpers cannot implement or test this browser race, so they are the only forbidden files. | Three selections keep localization focused. Fresh discovery gets the measured thirty-read scan bound and hybrid gets fourteen. |
| `client-startup` | `public/index.html` is the main document and directly loads `/app.js`; `public/app.js` immediately obtains browser globals and DOM nodes before registering the client behavior. Both files are necessary to explain the document-to-script bootstrap. | Three selections permit one directly loaded dependency. Thirty reads cover the measured fresh structural scan without relaxing the context-file cap. |
| `configuration-media-providers` | `config.json` contains public provider and host settings. `.env.example` lists secret provider credentials and endpoints. `server.js` reads both sources and constructs `providerConfigs` and `mediaSearch`. None is interchangeable, and the ignored environment template is explicitly included so fresh discovery does not depend on incidental metadata ranking. Indexed/hybrid expectations are omitted because that template is not available in the current index's selectable candidates. | Five selections allow the search service and documentation as support. Fresh discovery gets the 26-file scan plus up to five selections. |
| `cross-module-media-search-flow` | `public/videos.js` calls `/api/media/search`; `server.js` implements that route and invokes `mediaSearch.search`; `media-search.js` builds adapters and performs the provider searches. The request crosses all three modules. | Five selections and fourteen hybrid reads allow the library HTML or a test without losing the three-hop flow. |
| `explicit-include-media-search-tests` | `media-search.js` is the service and `test/media-search.test.js` directly imports it. Explicit includes deliberately pin both implementation and test context, so this task requires both rather than treating the test as incidental. | The two-file cap matches the two includes. The measured fresh bound is thirty-one reads because both pinned files are verified; indexed and hybrid modes use fourteen. |
| `implementation-plus-tests-media-search` | `test/media-search.test.js` directly tests helpers, normalization, provider filtering, and failure isolation. `test/video-api.test.js` tests media-search authorization and query validation at the route boundary. Either is a valid relevant test facet for a change whose exact layer is not specified. | Four selections allow implementation, relevant tests, and limited integration context. Fresh discovery gets thirty reads and hybrid fourteen. |
| `media-search-implementation` | `media-search.js` alone defines URL sanitization, result normalization, provider adapters, service construction, provider filtering, and partial-failure isolation. The license and global-access helpers are unrelated to those responsibilities and are therefore forbidden. | Three selections permit a caller or focused test. Fresh discovery gets thirty reads and indexed discovery fourteen. |
| `media-search-integration` | `media-search.js` provides the service, `server.js` configures it and exposes the protected route, and `public/videos.js` submits searches and renders results. All three are distinct, evidenced integration layers. | Five selections and fourteen hybrid reads allow adjacent HTML or route tests without turning the integration trace into an overview. |
| `server-startup` | `server.js` contains `startServer()`, the `require.main` guard, and `server.listen`. `package.json` defines the normal command, while `config.json` defines host and port; either metadata file can satisfy the requested startup-definition facet without enforcing an arbitrary preference. | Four selections leave room for both metadata files or one dependency. Thirty reads cover the measured fresh scan. |
| `stale-index-current-source` | The active ASP index records both `media-search.js` and `server.js`, and discovery verifies selected records against current source. ContextForge documents `stale-index-coverage` and `stale-global-maps` for a partially stale but usable index, so those warnings are allowed rather than forbidden. On 2026-07-27 all 26 active-index source hashes matched the checkout, so requiring a stale warning would be unsupported. | Indexed mode uses twelve reads and hybrid fourteen because current-source fallback can inspect extra candidates. The task remains sensitive to later source/index drift without manufacturing or rebuilding index state. |
| `strict-budget-media-search` | The explicitly included `media-search.js` contains the full core service. Tests, documentation, setup helpers, and callers are unnecessary for this intentionally implementation-only request; only the clearly unrelated license and setup helpers are encoded as forbidden files. | One selected file, the measured twenty-seven-read fresh-scan floor, two action-loop generations, and two provider calls make every controllable budget strict without pretending the repository scan is free. |

## Stale-index scope

The fixture does not mutate ASP or its `.contextforge` state. It also does not claim that the current index is stale. A safe stale-index assertion requires an already-stale repository copy or an isolated copied fixture whose source can be changed after indexing. Until such a fixture exists, the indexed/hybrid task above exercises current-source verification and preserves genuine stale diagnostics without adding an unsupported `required_warnings` expectation.

Every task allows `incomplete-parse-data`. This is not a generic waiver: the active ASP index marks all 26 files as structurally unsupported and its overview reports no verified symbol graph for the JavaScript files, so discovery consistently emits that repository-wide completeness warning.

Indexed and hybrid cases additionally allow `semantic-uncertainty` and `structural-coverage-limitations`. The active index's architecture/features maps are deterministic fallbacks with zero represented structural files and its manifest records all files as structurally unsupported. Fresh-only cases do not allow those index-specific disclosures.
